content: Topical gentamicin can cause severe allergic reactions. If you experience any of the following symptoms, stop using the medication immediately and seek medical attention: difficulty breathing or wheezing, a rapid heartbeat, fever or a general feeling of being unwell, swollen lymph nodes, swelling of the face, lips, mouth, tongue, or throat, trouble swallowing or a sensation of throat tightness, itching, skin rash, or hives (pale red bumps on the skin), nausea or vomiting, dizziness, lightheadedness, fainting, stomach cramps, or joint pain. Additionally, using topical gentamicin may lead to secondary infections caused by other microorganisms, such as fungi. Precautions: Who should not use topical gentamicin? Individuals who are allergic to gentamicin or any of the ingredients in the specific product should not use topical gentamicin. Your pharmacist can provide a complete list of ingredients in the product. Important Information Before Using Topical Gentamicin Do not use topical gentamicin unless it has been prescribed by a healthcare provider. Use the medication exactly as prescribed and do not share it with others, even if they have the same condition, as it may harm them. Keep topical gentamicin out of the reach of children. This medication is for external use only and should not be applied to the eyes. If you are using topical gentamicin to treat impetigo, remove any crusts before application to allow the antibiotic to reach the infection site effectively. What to Tell Your Healthcare Provider Inform your healthcare provider about all your health conditions and any medications, vitamins, minerals, herbal products, or supplements you are taking. This information will help determine if topical gentamicin is appropriate for you. Specifically, discuss the following: Pregnancy: It is not known if topical gentamicin can affect pregnancy or harm an unborn baby. Inform your provider if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. They will advise whether you should use this medication during pregnancy. Breastfeeding: It is unknown if topical gentamicin passes into breast milk. Drug Interactions There are no known interactions between topical gentamicin and foods, drinks, or other medications. However, it is unclear if alcohol consumption affects the medication. Overdose If you or someone else uses too much topical gentamicin, seek medical help immediately. Call 911 or contact a Poison Control Center at 800-222-1222. Missed Dose If you miss a dose, apply it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not use double or extra doses. It is important to complete the full prescribed course of topical gentamicin, even if your symptoms improve or resolve, to reduce the risk of future infections becoming resistant to this or similar medications.
